source.title: Uncovering Intermediate Variables in Transformers using Circuit Probing
source.authors: Michael A. Lepori; Thomas Serre; Ellie Pavlick

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests delayed generalization and gradual circuit development on a small algorithmic task, using circuit probing and causal abstraction rather than the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: Experiment 3 reports the model’s grokking curve and probes for a² during training. It does not vary training-set size. The b² selectivity analysis concerns an irrelevant variable, not removal of a memorizing component.
record.test_reason: Experiment 3 trains a 1-layer transformer on (a²+b) mod 113 with 33.3% training data and reports its own grokking curve. It also tracks a² circuit formation over training with circuit probing and causal abstraction (DAS). This is a different method aimed at the progress-measure question of Nanda et al. The paper is mainly a methods paper, but these trajectories are its own results on V1 and V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that the authors frame Experiment 3 as reproducing Nanda et al.'s finding in a different setting: the generalizing circuit forms continuously and is complete before generalization, but is not present from the outset. They also argue that linear and nonlinear probes and amnesic probing misleadingly imply the variable is present or causal from the start.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a 1-layer GPT2 trained on (a²+b) mod 113 and tracks a hypothesized intermediate variable with learned neuron masks, nearest-neighbor evaluation, and causal analysis; it does not reproduce the original grokking experiment’s task and mechanistic analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported training trajectory depends on the measurement method: circuit probing shows gradual development, while linear and nonlinear probes indicate near-immediate decodability.
record.problems: The training-set-size dependence is not tested. The training and test accuracy curves and some probe trajectories are figure-only, with no uncertainty estimates stated. The paper notes that ablating the b² circuit also harms performance even though its probe results indicate that b² is not computed, making that ablation difficult to interpret.
record.rows_left_out: No additional Experiment 3 results were left out that directly test these versions. The b² selectivity and ablation analyses are not evidence about removal of a memorizing component.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size (only 33.3% is used).
Later removal of memorizing components; Fourier-specific mechanism; cleanup phase.
All (the GPT2 experiments analyse pretrained models, not delayed generalization).
All (weight decay is used but not varied).

missing.what: Circuit-probing ablation trajectory over training. Ablating the a² circuit in attention destroys performance, but so does ablating the non-computing b² circuit, which weakens the causal reading of the circuit-probe result for V2.
MLP-block probe trajectories are chaotic for all methods, so the a² circuit is localized to attention.

record.verdict_notes: Primarily a methods paper that uses grokking as a validation case. Evidence comes from one model and seed, with no uncertainty reported and mostly figure-only values. The comparator probes (r4, r5) also decode the irrelevant b² at 100%, which is why they cannot speak to V2. The b² selectivity analysis is a control, not evidence on memorization removal.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not compare different training-set sizes, so it does not test whether smaller sets require more optimization.
It tracks a² circuit development and causal relevance, but does not test whether memorizing components are removed later.
No non-algorithmic data or initialization-scale/weight-norm sweep is tested.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning delayed-generalization result is tested.
No efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking test is reported.
The paper does not compare algorithms learned across runs.
The paper does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifact explanations.
